[[File:ELCochranJrAPL.jpg|thumb|Edward L Cochran Jr. in his laboratory at the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory]]

'''Edward Leo Cochran Jr.''' (March 18, 1929 – November 16, 2025) was an American chemist known for his work with [[free radicals]]. In 1956, he moved from [[Orange, Connecticut]], to Clarksville, Maryland, and began his career at [[Applied Physics Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=Ellicott City Events |date=January 29, 1956 |id={{ProQuest|540715285}} |page=B21}}</ref>  He also served as the second [[county executive]] of [[Howard County, Maryland]].<ref>{{cite book |title=New City Upon a Hill: A History of Columbia, Maryland |first1=Joseph R. |last1=Mitchell |first2=David |last2=Stebenne |page=112}}</ref>

==Background==
Cochran was born on March 18, 1929.<ref name="msa">{{Cite web |title=Edward L. Cochran Jr., County Executive, Howard County, Maryland |url=https://msa.maryland.gov/msa/mdmanual/36loc/how/former/html/msa14142.html |access-date=November 20, 2025 |date=November 18, 2025 |website=Maryland Manual On-Line |publisher=[[Maryland State Archives]]}}</ref> He graduated with a B.S. from [[List of Loyola University Maryland people|Loyola University]] in 1949. He achieved a master's degree in chemistry from [[Duquesne University]] in 1951 with a thesis on Basicities of Various Hydrazones.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://archive.org/details/duquesneuniversi40duqu/page/n88/mode/1up?q=%22Basicities+of+Various+Hydrazones%22 |title=Graduate Degrees Granted |journal=Duquesne University Bulletin 1952–1953 |publisher=[[Duquesne University]] |date=1952 |page=83}}</ref> He earned his PhD from the [[University of Notre Dame]] with a thesis on the photolysis of the alkyl iodides in the liquid phase.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=Howard's new executive: Reason to rule him, Cochran says |first=Michael J. |last=Clark |date=December 2, 1974 |id={{ProQuest|538722305}} |pages=C1, C2}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=University of Notre Dame Commencement |website=Archives of the University of Notre Dame |publisher=[[University of Notre Dame]] |url=http://www.archives.nd.edu/Commencement/1954-06-06_Commencement.pdf |access-date=December 22, 2013 |date=June 6, 1954}}</ref>

Cochran worked for the [[Applied Physics Laboratory]] as a chemist for most of his career except for the period which he was County Executive of Howard County, Maryland.<ref>{{cite news |first=Susan |last=DeFord |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=September 12, 2001 |title=As Keeper of County's Past, Activist Helps Shape Future; Preservation Group's President Uses Political Savvy, Civic Skills |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/2001/09/13/as-keeper-of-countys-past-activist-helps-shape-future/d932450d-87d4-48cc-a3c5-64df893d2e91/ |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251120223639/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/2001/09/13/as-keeper-of-countys-past-activist-helps-shape-future/d932450d-87d4-48cc-a3c5-64df893d2e91/ |archive-date=November 20, 2025 |id={{ProQuest|1965238358}} |page=HO1}}</ref> As chemist, Cochran was part of a team that carried out pioneering studies on the nature of free radicals, along with [[Chih-Kung Jen]], Frank. J. Adrian, Vernon A. Bowers, Samuel Foner, and others, including the description of the [[Electron Spin Resonance]] spectra of simple free radicals trapped in solid matrices at cryogenic temperatures.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v40/i1/p213_s1?isAuthorized=no |title = ESR Study of Ethynyl and Vinyl Free Radicals {{pipe}} Browse – Journal of Ch... |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130630042106/http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v40/i1/p213_s1?isAuthorized=no |archive-date=June 30, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Dozens of free radicals were described for the first time, including hydrogen, deuterium, nitrogen, methane, alkyl, formyl, ethynyl and vinyl, NH<sup>2</sup> and ND<sup>2</sup> and cyanogen and Methylene Imino.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v36/i7/p1938_s1 |title=ESR Detection of the Cyanogen and Methylene Imino Free Radicals {{pipe}} Browse – Journal of Chemical Physics |access-date=July 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130704183136/http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v36/i7/p1938_s1 |archive-date=July 4, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v32/i4/p963_s1 |title=Multiple Trapping Sites for Hydrogen Atoms in Rare Gas Matrices {{pipe}} Browse – Journal of Chemical Physics |access-date=July 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130704183139/http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v32/i4/p963_s1 |archive-date=July 4, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | bibcode = 1958PhRv..112.1169J | title=Electron Spin Resonance of Atomic and Molecular Free Radicals Trapped at Liquid Helium Temperature | journal=Physical Review | volume=112 | page=1169 | year=1958 |author1=Jen, C. K. |author2=Foner, S. N. |author3=Cochran, E. L. |author4=Bowers, V. A. | issue=4 | doi=10.1103/physrev.112.1169}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v34/i4/p1161_s1 |title=Anisotropic Hyperfine Interactions in the ESR Spectra of Alkyl Radicals {{pipe}} Browse - Journal of Chemical Physics |access-date=July 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130704183137/http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v34/i4/p1161_s1 |archive-date=July 4, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v40/i1/p213_s1 |title=ESR Study of Ethynyl and Vinyl Free Radicals {{pipe}} Browse – Journal of Chemical Physics |access-date=June 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130704183110/http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v40/i1/p213_s1 |archive-date=July 4, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://prl.aps.org/abstract/PRL/v1/i3/p91_1 |title=Phys. Rev. Lett. 1, 91 (1958) – Electron Spin Resonance Spectra of the NH<sub>2</sub> and ND<sub>2</sub> Free Radicals at 4.2K |publisher=Prl.aps.org |date=August 1, 1958 |access-date=July 1, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v36/i6/p1661_s1 |title=ESR Spectrum and Structure of the Formyl Radical {{pipe}} Browse – Journal of Chemical Physics |access-date=July 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130704183105/http://jcp.aip.org/resource/1/jcpsa6/v36/i6/p1661_s1 |archive-date=July 4, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Their paper on electron spin resonance proved to be one of the most frequently cited APL publications into the 21st century.<ref>{{Cite journal | url=https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.112.1169 | doi=10.1103/PhysRev.112.1169| title=Electron Spin Resonance of Atomic and Molecular Free Radicals Trapped at Liquid Helium Temperature| year=1958| last1=Jen| first1=C. K.| last2=Foner| first2=S. N.| last3=Cochran| first3=E. L.| last4=Bowers| first4=V. A.| journal=Physical Review| volume=112| issue=4| pages=1169–1182| bibcode=1958PhRv..112.1169J| url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=Walter G. |last1=Berl |date=1996 |title=Chih Kung Jen—A Remembrance |journal=Johns Hopkins APL Technical Digest |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=330–332 |url=https://secwww.jhuapl.edu/techdigest/content/techdigest/pdf/V17-N03/17-03-Berl.pdf}}</ref>

Following his term as County Executive, Cochran returned as spokesman for the Applied Physics Laboratory, and learned how to fly at [[Haysfield Airport]].<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=Cochran going back |date=November 29, 1978 |first=Micheal J. |last=Clark |id={{ProQuest|542149400}} |page=C2}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=Clarksville's Basslers say goodbye to family farm, Haysfield Airport |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2013/12/19/clarksvilles-basslers-say-goodbye-to-family-farm-haysfield-airport/ |date=December 19, 2013 |first=Janene |last=Holzberg |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607035523/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2013/12/19/clarksvilles-basslers-say-goodbye-to-family-farm-haysfield-airport/ |archive-date=June 7, 2025}}</ref> Cochran's family has remained active in Howard County. His son William is an active artist with works proposed for [[Merriweather Post Pavilion|Symphony Woods]], his daughter [[Courtney Watson (politician)|Courtney Watson]] became a school board member, County Councilperson, and Maryland State Delegate.<ref name=SunEulogy>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=Cochran making a sound contribution to his hometown of Columbia; Renowned artist creates multi-horn concept for Symphony Woods |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2014/03/02/cochran-making-a-sound-contribution-to-his-hometown-of-columbia-3/ |date=March 2, 2014 |first=Janene |last=Holzberg |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106220743/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2014/03/02/cochran-making-a-sound-contribution-to-his-hometown-of-columbia-3/ |archive-date=January 6, 2026 |id={{ProQuest|1504180604}} |page=G1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |first=April |last=Santana |date=November 18, 2025 |title=Howard's 2nd County Executive Edward Cochran dies at 96 |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2025/11/18/howard-county-executive-cochran-dies/ |access-date=November 18, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |language=en-US |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118170828/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2025/11/18/howard-county-executive-cochran-dies/ |archive-date=November 18, 2025}}</ref> His daughter Mary Catherine is a founding member of Preservation Howard County, winning the preservationist of the year award for defending and preserving the remaining county historical resources after significant losses to land development approved by the county.<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=The keepers of Howard County history |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2014/08/21/the-keepers-of-howard-county-history/ |first=Allison |last=Eatough |date=August 21, 2014 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106220312/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2014/08/21/the-keepers-of-howard-county-history/ |archive-date=January 6, 2026}}</ref>

Cochran died on November 16, 2025, at the age of 96.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Engel |first=Amanda |date=November 18, 2025 |title=Former Howard County Executive Edward Cochran dies at 96 |url=https://www.wmar2news.com/news/region/howard-county/former-howard-county-executive-edward-cochran-dies-at-96 |access-date=November 19, 2025 |website=WMAR 2 News Baltimore |language=en}}</ref>

== Political activity ==
Cochran served part-time as a member of the [[Howard County Public School System|Howard County Board of Education]] (1964–1968) becoming chairman and as a Howard County Councilperson (1971–1974).<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Afro-American]] |date=January 6, 1968 |title=Dr. Goedeke named to Howard County Post |id={{ProQuest|532228626}} |pages=32, 7}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=Councilmember Courtney Watson expected to announce Howard County executive run |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2013/09/09/councilmember-watson-expected-to-announce-howard-county-executive-run/ |date=September 9, 2013 |first=Amanda |last=Yeager |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127065932/https://www.baltimoresun.com/news/maryland/howard/ellicott-city/ph-ho-cf-watson-announcement,0,3891176.story#ixzz2e6X8xqqj |archive-date=November 27, 2024 |id={{ProQuest|1431063268}} |url-status=live |page=G1}}</ref> Cochran served as Howard County Executive (1974–1978), running on a slate of Columbia Democratic Club sponsored representatives from Columbia including Ginny Thomas, Lloyd Knowles, Richard Anderson and [[Ruth U. Keeton]].<ref>{{cite book |title=New City Upon a Hill |first1=Joseph R. |last1=Mitchell |first2=David |last2=Stebenne |page=112}}</ref> He was a member of the Regional Planning Council (1974–1978) and of the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board, (1977–1980).<ref name="msa" /> Other activities include: Board of Appeals candidate (1980),<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |title=Former Howard executive Cochran tries for position on county board of appeals |date=September 23, 1980 |id={{ProQuest|538091473}} |page=C2}}</ref> Howard County Task Force on growth and development (1988),<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |title=Task Force Scratching The Surface: Consensus on Growth Just the Beginning |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1988/07/14/task-force-scratching-the-surface/bc78ed26-8568-4fee-a146-1ecc094d82b2/ |date=July 14, 1988 |first=Lisa |last=Leff |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251120225709/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1988/07/14/task-force-scratching-the-surface/bc78ed26-8568-4fee-a146-1ecc094d82b2/ |archive-date=November 20, 2025 |id={{ProQuest|139528416}} |pages=Md1, Md5}}</ref> and Howard County Charter Review Commission (2012).<ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Howard County Times]] |title=Panel says no to suggested eminent domain charter amendment |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2011/11/10/panel-says-no-to-suggested-eminent-domain-charter-amendment/ |first=Lindsey |last=McPherson |date=November 10, 2011 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250608045909/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2011/11/10/panel-says-no-to-suggested-eminent-domain-charter-amendment/ |archive-date=June 8, 2025}}</ref>

=== Human rights ===

==== Desegregation of Howard County Schools ====
The Howard County School Board had pursued a policy of voluntary integration prior to 1964, which resulted in only a fraction of black students attending white schools.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |url=http://archives.explorehoward.com/news/6008414/triumphs-ruling-still-resonate-after-50-years/#ixzz2XAOtiWLo |title=Archived copy |work=explorehoward.com |access-date=July 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520071158/http://archives.explorehoward.com/news/6008414/triumphs-ruling-still-resonate-after-50-years/#ixzz2XAOtiWLo |archive-date=May 20, 2018 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> As late as 1964, ten years after [[Brown v. Board of Education]], the board stated that it would not consider forcing integration until 1967, to "allow for a reasonable period of adjustment" to the change.<ref name=":0" /> However, in May 1964, as the county experienced increasing growth, the board was expanded to five members, and Cochran was appointed as one of the board's new members.<ref name="DeFord">{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A21091-2004May12.html |title=Difficult Change, One Step at a Time |first=Susan |last=DeFord |date=May 13, 2004 |page=HO16 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=July 2, 2022 |id={{ProQuest|409626578}}}}</ref> He is credited by Maryland State Senator [[Robert Kittleman]], then the education chairman of Howard County's [[NAACP]] chapter, for providing the swing vote on February 9, 1965, to close all-black schools.<ref>{{cite news |first=Larry |last=Carson |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2004/02/01/a-struggle-for-equality-amid-a-legacy-of-racism/ |title=A struggle for equality amid a legacy of racism |newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=February 1, 2004 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106135926/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2004/02/01/a-struggle-for-equality-amid-a-legacy-of-racism/ |archive-date=January 6, 2026 |id={{ProQuest|406585189}} |page=1B}}</ref><ref name="DeFord" /><ref>{{cite news |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=May 13, 2004 |title=Bringing Innovation To Schools: Integration |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/2004/05/13/bringing-innovation-to-schools-integration/3cee31fe-6896-421e-a403-298a2c1bafba/ |first=Ylan Q. |last=Mui |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251120222615/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/2004/05/13/bringing-innovation-to-schools-integration/3cee31fe-6896-421e-a403-298a2c1bafba/ |archive-date=November 20, 2025 |id={{ProQuest|2459870525}} |page=HO21}}</ref>

===== Human Rights Act =====
In 1975, as County Executive, Dr. Cochran introduced an act establishing an Office of Human Rights and making discrimination on the basis of race, creed, religion, physical or mental handicap, color, sex, national origin, age, occupation, marital status, political opinion, sexual orientation, or personal appearance in the areas of housing, employment, law enforcement, public accommodations, and financing unlawful in Howard County Maryland.<ref>[https://apps.howardcountymd.gov/olis/GetFile.aspx?id=23595 Howard County Council Bill 38, 1975].</ref>

==Awards==
In 2009, the Howard County Human Rights Commission awarded Cochran the 2009 Human Rights Award.<ref>{{cite web|title=2012 Human Rights Commission Award|url=http://www.howardcountymd.gov/displayprimary.aspx?id=6442470148|access-date=June 22, 2013}}</ref> In 2010 he was awarded the James Clark Jr. Medal from [[Howard County Community College]] for his role in growing Howard Community College as a member of the board of trustees.<ref>{{cite web|title=Howard Community College|url=http://www.howardcc.edu/about_hcc/pathways/Spring2011/campus_community.html|access-date=June 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141118110019/http://www.howardcc.edu/about_hcc/pathways/Spring2011/campus_community.html|archive-date=November 18, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
